summary: Webhook function-calls retried by platform on timeout leading to duplicate side-effects; guidance requested for idempotency
description: Issue summary: Customer reports duplicate side-effects (duplicate bank transfer hooks) when Redwood invokes their external webhook for function/tool calls. The external webhook occasionally times out; Redwood retries the webhook invocation which results in duplicate downstream actions because the webhook endpoint is not deduplicating on invocation id. Impact: customer observed 2-3 duplicate webhook hits for ~0.5% of calls during a 3-hour window, causing billing and operational risk. They have paused the integration and requested recommended idempotency patterns. Environment: Production: customer-private deployment (enterprise) in us-east. Using TypeScript SDK v1.8 to open streaming chat sessions with function_call hooks enabled. Steps to reproduce: 1) Configure a function in model manifest to call an external webhook URL. 2) Simulate occasional 5-10s processing delay on the webhook to force timeouts from Redwood side. 3) Observe multiple HTTP POSTs to webhook with different timestamps but same payload body. Expected: either a single invocation or a stable invocation identifier provided so receiver can dedupe. Observed: 1-3 POSTs, varying slightly in JSON body metadata leading to receiver not treating them as identical. Logs/IDs: customer provided sample webhook request bodies (anonymized) showing fields: "tool_name", "input", "timestamp", "attempt" (1,2), but no single stable invocation UUID in the payload. Customer asks: what is Redwood's recommended idempotency contract for function/webhook callbacks? Is there a header or field we can rely on? Can they configure the platform to include a stable invocation id?
steps_to_reproduce: Create model manifest with a function that uses webhook tool (url points to test receiver)
Start a chat session via TS SDK that triggers the function_call path
Add artificial 6-8s processing delay in receiver to trigger platform timeout/retry behavior
Inspect receiver logs for multiple POSTs and compare payloads/headers
logs: Gateway logs: connection to customer webhook timed out after 5s, platform retried according to backoff policy
comments: Customer: We saw duplicate bank transfer webhook posts. Our receiver doesn't have a dedupe key and the payload changes slightly between attempts, so we're getting double charges. Want a reliable unique id for each function invocation so we can make our webhook idempotent.

Support (Maya): Thanks for the report — assigning Diego from runtime to investigate. Can you paste a redacted example of the full request headers and body for both attempts? Also confirm whether you control the receiver code (yes/no).
Customer: Pasted headers. We control receiver (yes) and can persist request ids if provided. We do not want to rely on timestamps/attempt numbers.

Support (Diego): Initial hypothesis: platform retries webhook invocations on timeout/5xx and includes an "attempt" field but not a stable invocation UUID. We'll verify whether the runtime sends a consistent invocation_id header or field. If not, recommend receiver-side dedupe using stable id once we provide guidance or a workaround.

SRE (internal): We saw retries from gateway for pipeline X during the window. Retry logic uses exponential backoff and replays the original payload but currently does not inject a stable invocation_id header in older runtime builds.
investigation: Reproduced in staging with TS SDK v1.8 and runtime version 2026-02-28. Staging webhook receiver recorded two POSTs when simulating a 6s delay: both bodies identical except for 'attempt' field and timestamps. No 'invocation_id' present in headers or body.
Checked recent runtime change logs: a PR to add stable tool invocation ids landed behind a feature flag in 2026-03-04 but was not enabled for enterprise private deployments by default.
Confirmed that newer hosted deployments include header 'X-Redwood-Tool-Invocation-Id' and include 'tool_invocation_id' in payload; private deployments may need configuration or upgrade.
Risk assessment: Until stable invocation ids are present, receivers must dedupe on payload semantics or implement idempotency using business keys to avoid side-effects on retries.
Related items: linked internal ticket INT-1987 (runtime: enable toolkit invocation id feature flag for private deployments)
Related github PRs: PR-3456 (add invocation id header to webhook calls)
resolution: 1) Make receiver idempotent using business-level keys (e.g., customer transaction id included in function input) and persist processed ids to ignore duplicates.
2) If feasible, add a short-lived dedupe store keyed by a hash of request payload and business key for the window of potential retries (e.g., 30s).
3) Temporarily increase webhook timeout threshold on receiver to avoid platform-side retries while we enable the feature, or return 200 quickly and process asynchronously (ack pattern).
- Diego to coordinate enabling the stable invocation id feature flag for the customer's private deployment (INT-1987) and schedule an upgrade window (ETA 2026-03-18).

- SRE to confirm that once enabled, Redwood will include a header 'X-Redwood-Tool-Invocation-Id' and a top-level field 'tool_invocation_id' in webhook payloads for all subsequent invocations to support receiver-side dedupe.
Follow-up: After feature is enabled, customer should verify dedupe behavior and then re-open ticket if duplicates persist.
